description: The Energy Poverty Advisory Hub (EPAH), the leading EU initiative on local action against energy poverty, publishes an energy poverty indicators dashboard organised by topic for each European country, built from publicly available EU-wide datasets. Topics are climate (heating and cooling degree days, cold and heat stress days), facilities and housing (building stock indicators such as dwellings with energy label A, damp and leaks, heating systems, air conditioning and recent efficiency improvements), energy consumption and equipment, mobility, energy expenditure and prices, health (excess winter and summer mortality) and socio-economic living conditions such as arrears on utility bills and inability to keep homes warm or cool. Nine new indicators were recently added, alongside a report expanding energy poverty measurement to summer heat, and EPAH also runs technical assistance, country fiches and events. Coverage: EU member states and other European countries including Ukraine, Turkey and the Western Balkans. Access: free dashboard. Licence: Commission legal notice. Caveats: data gaps occur for some years and countries because of source timelines. Simulation uses are social vulnerability and housing condition indicators for heat, cold and retrofit equity studies. Related records: the LEAD Tool and the EU Building Stock Observatory.
